subject: music
topicDisplay: Areas Of Inquiry Music For Listening And Performance
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Gamelan music frequently uses 'interlocking' (kotekan) parts, meaning...?
options: The ensemble plays in strict Western major scales
All players double the same melody an octave apart
Two parts combine, each playing alternate notes, to create a single faster composite line
questions.explain: Interlocking parts dovetail, each playing alternate notes so that together they form one rapid composite line.

questions.q: In performance, 'interpretation' refers to...?
options: Transposing the music to a new key
The performer's expressive choices of dynamics, phrasing, tempo and articulation within the score
Playing the notes exactly as printed with no expressive choices
questions.explain: Interpretation is the performer's expressive shaping of dynamics, phrasing, tempo and articulation.

questions.q: The Latin American 'clave' is best described as...?
options: A characteristic two-bar rhythmic pattern underpinning many Afro-Cuban styles
questions.explain: The clave is a foundational two-bar rhythmic pattern that organises much Afro-Cuban and Latin music.

questions.q: A pivot chord in modulation is best defined as which of the following?
options: A chord borrowed from the parallel major
The final chord of a phrase only
A chromatic chord with no diatonic function
A chord common to both the old and new keys used to effect the change
questions.explain: A pivot chord belongs diatonically to both keys, smoothing the transition during a modulation.

questions.q: A 'reel', another Celtic dance type, is usually in...?
options: Simple quadruple time (4/4 or cut common) with a flowing quaver movement
questions.explain: The reel is a fast dance in simple quadruple time with continuous even quavers.

questions.q: The relative minor of G major is which key?
questions.explain: The relative minor shares the key signature of G major (one sharp) and is E minor.

questions.q: In Celtic folk music, a 'jig' is most commonly in which metre?
questions.explain: The jig is a lively dance typically in compound 6/8 time.

questions.q: A homophonic texture is characterised by which?
options: Two or more independent equal melodic lines
A melody supported by chordal accompaniment
questions.explain: Homophony features a principal melody accompanied by chords, all parts moving largely together.

questions.q: Augmentation as a melodic device involves which alteration?
options: Restating a theme with proportionally lengthened note values
Transposing a theme up an octave
Restating a theme with shortened note values
questions.explain: Augmentation lengthens the rhythmic values of a theme, typically doubling their duration.

questions.q: A 4-3 suspension resolves by which means?
options: The third rises to the fourth
The fourth steps down to the third
The fourth leaps up to the sixth
questions.explain: In a 4-3 suspension the dissonant fourth resolves downwards by step onto the consonant third.

questions.q: The Indonesian 'gamelan' is primarily an ensemble of...?
questions.explain: A gamelan is built chiefly from tuned metallophones, gongs and drums.

questions.q: An appoggiatura is best defined as which?
options: A dissonant note approached by leap and resolved by step
A note approached and left by step
questions.explain: An appoggiatura is an accented non-harmony note usually approached by leap and resolved by step.

questions.q: Which key signature has four sharps?
questions.explain: E major has four sharps: F sharp, C sharp, G sharp and D sharp.

questions.q: In the alap–jhor–jhalla–gat structure, the 'gat' section is distinguished by...?
options: The entry of the tabla and a fixed, composed melody with a regular tala
A solo drone with no melody
A return to the unmetred opening
questions.explain: The gat is the composed, metred section where the tabla enters and a fixed melody is set within a tala.

questions.q: In African music, the 'master drummer' typically...?
options: Leads the ensemble, signalling changes and improvising over the cyclic patterns
Sets up the instruments before the performance
questions.explain: The master drummer leads, cues changes and improvises over the underlying cyclic patterns.

questions.q: A Neapolitan sixth chord is a major triad built on which scale degree, usually in first inversion?
questions.explain: The Neapolitan sixth is a major triad on the flattened supertonic (flattened second degree), typically used in first inversion.

questions.q: A modulation from C major to G major is a move to which related key?
questions.explain: G major is the dominant key of C major, a closely related key with one extra sharp.

questions.q: Gamelan ensembles commonly use which two tuning systems?
questions.explain: Gamelan typically uses the five-note slendro and the seven-note pelog tuning systems.

questions.q: A secondary dominant such as V of V in C major would be which chord?
questions.explain: In C major, the dominant is G, and the dominant of G (V of V) is a D major chord.

questions.q: What characterises a cadential six-four chord?
options: A tonic chord in root position resolving to V
A second-inversion tonic chord on a strong beat resolving to V before the cadence
A dominant chord in third inversion
questions.explain: The cadential 6/4 is a second-inversion tonic chord on an accented beat that delays and decorates the dominant before the cadence.

questions.q: A passing note is which type of non-chord tone?
options: Approached by leap and left by step
A note that returns to its starting pitch
A sustained dissonance held over a barline
Approached and left by step in the same direction filling a melodic gap
questions.explain: A passing note connects two chord tones a third apart, approached and quitted by step in the same direction.

questions.q: In figured bass, the symbol '6' beneath a bass note indicates which chord position?
questions.explain: A bare '6' indicates a first-inversion triad, with the bass note a sixth and a third above it.

questions.q: In figured bass, the symbols '6/4' indicate which inversion of a triad?
questions.explain: A 6/4 figure denotes a second-inversion triad, with the fifth in the bass.

questions.q: In C major, the chord built on the leading note (vii) is which quality?
questions.explain: The triad on the leading note in a major key is diminished, comprising B-D-F in C major.

questions.q: A 'cyclic' or 'ostinato' pattern, common in African drumming, is...?
options: A short rhythmic or melodic pattern repeated continuously as a foundation
A pattern that constantly changes and never repeats
questions.explain: Cyclic patterns repeat a short rhythmic or melodic cell continuously, forming the music's foundation.

questions.q: The continuous sustained background pitch in Indian classical music, often provided by the tanpura, is called the...?
questions.explain: The drone is the sustained pitch (usually tonic and dominant) supplied by the tanpura beneath the melody.

questions.q: A circle-of-fifths progression characteristically moves the bass by which interval?
questions.explain: A circle-of-fifths sequence moves root by root down a fifth (equivalently up a fourth) each step.

questions.q: A Picardy third refers to which feature?
options: A minor-key piece ending on a major (raised third) tonic chord
A major piece ending on the minor third
A third added above the melody
A chord built on the third degree
questions.explain: A tierce de Picardie raises the third of the final tonic chord so a minor-key work ends on a major chord.

questions.q: In Indian classical music, a 'raga' is best defined as...?
options: The drone instrument that sustains the tonic
A melodic framework of notes and characteristic phrases used as the basis for improvisation
A fixed rhythmic cycle of beats
questions.explain: A raga is the melodic framework, comprising a set of notes and characteristic phrases, on which improvisation is built.

questions.q: In sub-Saharan African music, 'polyrhythm' refers to...?
options: The use of only one drum
The simultaneous combination of two or more contrasting rhythms
A gradual slowing of the pulse
A single rhythm played in unison by all performers
questions.explain: Polyrhythm layers two or more contrasting rhythms sounding at once, a defining feature of much African music.
